title: Learning solos and how to practice
summary: His method for transcribed solos and metronome practice.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: Well, you know, the young players should memorize everything the can. Now, not everybody can memorize, it's not easy. But there's a very lucky thing, there's an awful lot of solos transcribed now. And I know with my pupils, I give them a solo every week or every two weeks, of some famous solo, and I make them learn it like an etude. I say, don't come in here and bluff your way through it, learn that like you're practicing Arvins or ____, I don't give a damn. You learn that like an etude and I don't want you to come in here and try to sound like Freddie Hubbard or anybody else, sound like you, you know. I want you to take this solo and make it you not him. Because you're never going to play like that. Come in and play it your way because these are just notes. Forget what he sounds like.
And then I make them learn their chords on that solo, be able to play all the chords from that solo and all the scales associated with those chords. And then we pick another

solo.
Now, I think that's a good thing to do, even if you do copy solos. It's one thing to be able to sing along with a soloist, another thing to get it with your fingers. And you've got to practice to get it in your fingers. And I'm surprised, most people don't know how to practice. You know, you don't just make a mistake and go back and play three notes, oh, there it is, then you go ahead. If you make a mistake, I don't care if you had it perfect all week, you go back and you practice with a metronome, you set it at half the speed and move it up one notch at a time. And generally it comes out to about 20 times, until you get it up to the speed it should be. Then you go and play it through.
Now, if you make that mistake again, you do the same process. You don't say, oh, I know it, I just made a mistake. You never say, oh, I know it, I just made a mistake. And so if you do that, then you're going to have it in your fingers. Otherwise you've got what you call a b.s., a bullshit technique, you know. One time you can do it, another time you can't. But when you take it from half speed to full speed, you get control of your muscles. So your muscles respond to your mind and you improve your chances of getting it right, 100 percent.
